page: Amazon Web Services h1.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, accompanied by 45 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 4.0 GB per core ratio. Bundled local storage includes 8000 GB of high-capacity HDD storage, with baseline network connectivity operating at 12 Gbps. It does not include GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid multi-threaded performance offset by constrained single-threaded execution. In single-core tests such as Geekbench and stress-ng, processing power ranks in the lower 10 percent of evaluated instances. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 7383.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 28705.01, fall consistently within the mid-range spectrum. Large block memory read bandwidth operates at 52.11 GB/sec, though uncached large write throughput declines to a weaker 24.24 GB/sec.

The h1.8xlarge provides high resource density for sequential data access, offering substantial magnetic storage volume coupled with balanced compute at a predictable operational scale. Given the mechanical limits of the bundled HDD storage and modest single-core throughput, the instance is engineered for throughput-intensive data pipelines, MapReduce clusters, data warehousing, and log processing rather than low-latency transactional databases or intensive real-time computation.

This hardware profile delivers qualitative cost advantages for operations that require dense bulk storage alongside distributed processing, serving distributed big data clusters, batch processing, sequential data ingestion, and log analysis.
